item.title: What TLA+ can and can't check
item.description:
📝 P' ("P prime") is true if P is true in the next state. So if we check the property []P, that means that []P is true in every initial state, and then by the definition of "always" means that P is true in every future state from that initial state, meaning it is true in every state of every behavior. [](P => <>Q) is true if, for every state where P is true, there is a future state where Q is true.
🔗 Read more: https://buttondown.com/hillelwayne/archive/what-tla-can-and-cant-check/
